mutant.description: Two mutants run against scratch copies of STATE_MODEL.md (never against the committed file) to prove AC1 and AC2 CAN fail rather than being tautologies that any document would pass. Mutant A: truncated the file to its first 5 lines (the frontmatter paragraph only, before the Axis-1 table) and re-ran AC1's exact invocation. Mutant B: scripted every DENY-BY-DESIGN occurrence after the first down to a placeholder token and re-ran AC2's exact invocation.
mutant.expected: Mutant A must drop AC1's count below 6 (the truncated text carries at most one of the six ratified tokens in prose, not the six-row table). Mutant B must drop AC2's count to exactly 1, below the required 2.
mutant.observed: Mutant A: grep -c -E 'CHECKED|BLIND|INERT|COARSE|UNCHECKED|DENY-BY-DESIGN' on the 5-line truncation returned 1 (would FAIL AC1's >=6 bound). Mutant B: grep -c 'DENY-BY-DESIGN' on the singleton-reduced copy returned 1 (would FAIL AC2's >=2 bound). Both mutants fired as designed; neither check is satisfiable by an empty or trivial document.
